title: Put inventory & labor on CA_3 and other CA volume stores
body: CA_3 leads the panel at 2,923 units in the last 28 days. CA drives the largest share of demand — protect on-hands and weekend staffing there before thinner markets.

title: Ride FOODS SNAP days (+9% units)
body: FOODS average units rise about 9% on SNAP benefit days (largest state lifts: WI +14%, TX +10%, CA +7%). Time endcaps, ads, and backroom replenishment to each state’s SNAP calendar — not a flat national week.

title: Close the under-forecast gap before it becomes empty shelves
body: Across the latest 28-day outlook, actual demand exceeded the signal by +495 units network-wide. Top gaps: WI_1/FOODS (+99), CA_2/FOODS (+93), CA_3/FOODS (+73). Raise safety stock / earlier POs for those store×category cells.

title: Treat HOBBIES as intermittent — don’t plan shelves like FOODS
body: Zero-sale day share averages FOODS 58%, HOBBIES 76%, HOUSEHOLD 75%. FOODS is 45% of recent units; HOBBIES needs flexible facings and slower replenishment cadence, not FOODS-style continuous flow.

title: Put temporary price investment on HOBBIES first
body: Within the same SKU, low-price weeks sell a median +12% more units than high-price weeks for HOBBIES (70% of those SKUs respond positively). Category summary: HOBBIES +12% (responders 70%) · FOODS +7% (responders 68%) · HOUSEHOLD -2% (responders 38%). WoW cuts ≥5%: FOODS +0% units when cut ≥5% · HOBBIES +34% units when cut ≥5% · HOUSEHOLD +0% units when cut ≥5%. Fund markdowns where within-SKU response is strongest — not as blanket network discounts.
